acceptance_criteria: Every valid schema probe round-trips deterministically.
Every invalid schema probe produces the expected typed finding or blocked transition.
Branch-local state and mutually exclusive facts remain distinguishable.
Assertions, testimony, beliefs, uncertainty, and accepted facts remain distinguishable.
Story time, presentation order, publication time, and revision time remain explicit.
Adaptation branches cannot mutate source canon.
Shared-canon changes require explicit authority and versioned dependency handling.
Deep hierarchy preserves stable identity independently of display numbering or ordering.
Corrections and retractions preserve historical publication evidence.
Rights expiry or withdrawal invalidates only affected future uses, packages, and approvals.
No schema probe requires a property-specific storage fork.
Any proposed generic primitive is justified by at least two materially different fixture needs or is explicitly documented as a narrowly necessary foundational concept.
Probe coverage is machine-readable (fixtures/registry.json) and enforced in CI.
evidence_expected: Probe directories with valid/invalid cases and expected findings; contract-validator runs in CI.
limitations: Completed 2026-07-28: all eight probes implemented with valid/invalid cases, PROBE.md core-vs-template statements, checksums, and CI-enforced registry coverage; contributes evidence to GATE-0003 (DEC-0008).
plan_items.objective: Formalize and execute compact schema probes for branching, contested truth, nonlinear chronology, adaptation, shared canon, deep hierarchy, evidence correction, and rights change against the F1 contracts, proving that the generic domain model can represent materially different narrative architectures without commerce, runtime, or genre-specific contamination.
